entities.evidence: Cain, Eve’s son and Abel’s brother, responds to the punishment Yahweh has just pronounced for killing Abel.
אֶל יַהְוֶה names Yahweh as the God whom Cain addresses after hearing his sentence. The LORD source tag confirms the identification.

analysis.evidence: קַיִן is the speaker, אֶל־יַהְוֶה identifies the addressee, and גָּדוֹל עֲונִי מִנְּשֹׂא gives Cain’s words directly.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for Cain with its etymology left open pending evidence.
draft.definition: Cain, the son of Adam and Eve and brother of Abel.
draft.evidence: Genesis 4:1 names Eve’s son קַיִן. Genesis 4:2 identifies Abel as his brother and names Cain again when describing his work.

analysis.evidence: In וַיֹּאמֶר קַיִן אֶל יַהְוֶה, קַיִן names the speaker, and אֶל יַהְוֶה identifies whom he addresses.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper noun, with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: The personal name of Abel’s brother.

draft.change: Add Gen.9.8 as evidence for the existing addressee sense of אֶל at word index 0.
draft.definition: With a verb of speaking, אֶל introduces the addressee.
draft.evidence: In Gen.9.8, וְאֶל בָּנָיו adds Noah’s sons to the hearers already introduced by אֶל נֹחַ.

analysis.evidence: In וַיֹּאמֶר קַיִן אֶל יַהְוֶה, “Cain said to YHWH,” אֶל introduces YHWH as the addressee of Cain’s speech.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew preposition without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Marks the person or people addressed.

analysis.evidence: וַיֹּאמֶר קַיִן אֶל יַהְוֶה means “Cain said to Yahweh.” The preposition אֶל introduces יַהְוֶה as the person Cain addresses.
analysis.morphology: Singular proper noun without a prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Personal name of the God of Israel

analysis.evidence: גָּדוֹל is the predicate of עֲונִי, “my guilt” or “my punishment.” מִנְּשֹׂא expresses the limit exceeded, “too great to bear.” Cain is describing the severity of his burden.
analysis.morphology: Predicative adjective, masculine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: Cain has just heard his sentence. In גָּדוֹל עֲונִי מִנְּשֹׂא, he describes it as too great to bear. Although עָוֺן can also mean guilt, Cain’s next words about exile and the danger of being killed favor the punishment sense.
analysis.morphology: Singular common-gender noun in the construct state with a first-person common singular possessive suffix.

analysis.evidence: In גָּדוֹל עֲוֹנִי מִנְּשֹׂא, גָּדוֹל sets up a comparison, and מִן introduces the infinitive. Cain says his punishment is too great for him to bear.
analysis.morphology: Qal infinitive construct with prefixed מִן
